title: Smart Contracts, EVM & Consensus Protocols
description: Explore programmable blockchains, EVM bytecode, Merkle trees, and Proof of Stake consensus.

questions.question: What is a 'Smart Contract' on a programmable blockchain?
options: Self-executing code stored on the blockchain with terms directly written into code
A legal document signed with an electronic stylus and saved as a PDF
An insurance policy purchased through a web browser extension
An encrypted email exchange between corporate attorneys

questions.question: What cryptographic data structure enables rapid, tamper-evident verification of transaction inclusion in a block?
options: Merkle Tree
Binary Search Tree
Doubly Linked List
Circular FIFO Queue

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Proof-of-Work (PoW) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus mechanisms?
options: PoW relies on intensive computational energy, while PoS validators commit capital (tokens) as collateral
PoS requires dedicated ASIC mining rigs in massive server farms
PoW cannot be used for decentralized cryptocurrencies
PoS executes zero transactions per second

questions.question: What is 'Gas' in the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)?
options: A computational metering unit paying for the CPU and storage resources consumed by transaction execution
The physical cooling fluid circulating inside validator server racks
An encrypted session identifier for Web3 browser extensions
A proprietary token used only for database backups

questions.question: What vulnerability occurs when an external contract call allows execution flow to re-enter before state balances update?
options: Reentrancy Attack
Flash Loan Arbitrage
Integer Truncation
Sybil Collision
